title: The stone didn’t just roll away… your excuse did too.
paragraphs: The stone didn’t just roll away… your excuse did too.
Let that sit.
Because if the tomb is empty, then your “I can’t change” is already buried.
And most people don’t want to face that.

We love a Savior who died.
But we struggle with a Savior who rose.
Why?

Because a dead Jesus asks for sympathy.
A risen Jesus demands surrender.
Ephesians 1:19–20 doesn’t whisper this truth—it shouts it:

“...the immeasurable greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of His great might that He worked in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places.”
Read that again.
The same power.

Not a lesser version.
Not a diluted form.
Not a future promise only.
The same power that raised Jesus from the dead is already at work in those who believe.
So here’s the tension…

If that power is real—
why are so many still living like the grave has the final word?

Still bound to secret sin.
Still drowning in shame.
Still addicted to what Christ already defeated.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because the resurrection doesn’t just comfort you…
It confronts you.
You say, “I’m too far gone.”
But Scripture says:
“If the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you… He who raised Christ Jesus… will also give life to your mortal bodies.” — Romans 8:11
You say, “I’ve tried and failed too many times.”
But the Word says:
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
You say, “This is just who I am.”
But Jesus says:
“So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.” — John 8:36
So now the real question isn’t…
“Is God powerful enough?”
The empty tomb already answered that.
The real question is:
Will you believe enough to step out of what’s already dead?
Because some of us are sitting in open tombs.

Door wide open.
Light pouring in.
But we’re still hugging the darkness like it’s home.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Not to shame you.
But to call you out.

The Gospel is not behavior modification.
It’s resurrection transformation.

You were not slightly broken—you were dead in sin (Ephesians 2:1).
Not weak. Not struggling. Dead.
But Jesus…

Lived the life you couldn’t live.
Died the death you deserved.
And on the third day—He walked out of the grave.

Victory in His lungs.
Authority in His scars.
Power in His name.
And now?
“God… made us alive together with Christ… and raised us up with Him…” — Ephesians 2:4–6
Did you catch that?
Not just forgiven.
Raised.
Not just saved from hell.
Brought into life.
Not just cleaned up.
Made new.
So why are you negotiating with chains that Jesus already shattered?
Why are you calling “normal” what Christ died to destroy?
Why are you entertaining darkness when resurrection light is already yours?
This is your wake-up call.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you feel ready.
Not when life gets easier.
Now.
Repent.
Turn from sin—not slowly, not casually—but decisively.
Run to Jesus.

Not with polished words.
Not with fake strength.
But with honest surrender.
Because grace is not permission to stay buried.
Grace is the power to rise.
And hear me clearly—
You don’t resurrect yourself.
Jesus does.

You bring your dead places.
He brings His life.

You bring your surrender.
He brings His Spirit.

You bring your nothing.
He gives you everything.
So today…

Stop rehearsing your past.
Stop defending your bondage.
Stop shrinking your calling.
The tomb is empty.
Which means your story isn’t over.

Which means your addiction is not final.
Your shame is not permanent.
Your failure is not fatal.
Jesus is alive.
And because He lives—
You can rise.
You can walk free.
You can become who God actually called you to be.
But don’t just feel this.
Respond.
We don’t preach self-help.
We proclaim a risen King.
And His power didn’t stay in the tomb.
It’s calling your name.
